questions.question: Profit rose from ₹14.83 crore in FY24 to ₹25.90 crore in FY26, but only 35.2% of operating profit came in as cash. What does that suggest?

choices.text: The business is doing brilliantly; cash doesn't matter.
Some profit may be stuck in unpaid bills or unsold goods, so check how fast customers pay.
The company must have paid a big dividend.
Profit and cash are always equal, so the figures must be wrong.

questions.explanation: Profit is counted when a sale is made; cash arrives when the customer pays. For Monomark Engineering (India) Limited, only 35.2% of operating profit turned into cash, so money is getting stuck. Trade receivables and inventory are where to look.

questions.question: At the top price, Monomark Engineering (India) Limited's P/E is 16.9x. Similar listed companies have a P/E of about 27.6x. What does that tell you?

choices.text: It costs about the same as, or less than, similar companies for each rupee of profit.
It costs more than similar companies for each rupee of profit, so its profit must grow faster to be worth it.
The P/E shows how many shares the company has.

questions.explanation: A P/E of 16.9x against 27.6x means you pay no more for each rupee of Monomark Engineering (India) Limited's profit than for its peers'. That is a fair starting point, not a guarantee.
